cards.hearing: You may be hearing that the Fed, which sets short-term interest rates, just raised them again.
cards.why: That can nudge up costs like mortgages and car loans, so borrowing money for a house or a big purchase can feel a little more expensive for a while.
cards.but: But rates moving is normal, and your plan already expected that rates would not sit still forever.
cards.story: Think of a thermostat in a house. Someone bumps it up a notch and the family does not call a moving truck. The rooms are the same. It is an adjustment, not a new house.
say: Interest rates can move and your plan can stay put.
We built this plan knowing rates would shift. This is not a reason to rebuild the house.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing mixed signals, stocks were up a bit heading into the weekend, but the early read this morning looks a touch softer.
cards.why: That kind of back and forth is just markets digesting news over the weekend, it does not mean much for your day to day life or your long-term goals.
cards.but: But small wobbles like this happen all the time, and reacting to every one of them is not a strategy, it is a distraction.
cards.story: Picture checking the weather every hour before a trip that is still three weeks away. The forecast changes, but the trip date does not move. Your plan works the same way, it is not rebuilt every morning.
say: A soft morning does not change a long-term plan.
We stay focused on the trip, not the hourly forecast.
